\section{How Branch Inventories Reduce to CM Obligations}

This appendix explains how the large branch inventory collapses to a small number of CM obligations.  The reader should be able to see the proof role without inspecting every source row.  Each family below states the same mathematical question in a different terminal setting: what is the selected record \(Q\), which class datum is being tested, and which face closes the fail branch?

\subsection{Field-face terminal obligations}

The largest family consists of terminal source walls, source reserves, source pulses, square-source windows, receiver defects, finite-difference defects, endpoint readout defects, and Zeno source residues.  In these cases carrier and participation have survived far enough for the proof to ask the final question: does one positive scale carry the field coherently?

The retained-Pack-and-Part Field statement is
\[
  \Pack_Q\wedge\Part_{N,Q}\wedge\forall r>0\,\neg\Field_{N,r,Q}
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \Exit(Q;\Owork).
\]
The proof is short because the work is in the face order.  Pack supplies the same-fluid carrier.  Part supplies the same Navier--Stokes participation tower.  The remaining continuation requirement is the positive-scale field readout.  When every \(r>0\) fails, the branch exits through Field.

This is the family used by retained pulses and annular source residues after selection.  The page should read these branches as failed positive-scale readability.  The proof force comes from the lost coherent field scale, not from the mere presence of a large quantity.

\subsection{Finite Pack/Part/Field disjunction obligations}

Some branch surfaces produce a finite list of same-solution alternatives rather than a single named face.  The proof then runs the Pack-first test on each alternative.  Every alternative lands in one of the three displayed losses:
\[
  \neg\Pack_Q,\qquad
  \Pack_Q\wedge\neg\Part_{N,Q},\qquad
  \Pack_Q\wedge\Part_{N,Q}\wedge\forall r>0\,\neg\Field_{N,r,Q}.
\]
A finite disjunction of these losses is still exhausted by the same witness tree.  Once the alternatives are exhausted, no extra terminal branch remains outside the pass-or-exit law.

This family turns case lists into a finite proof obligation.  The list is finite, and each item has the same closing obligation: select the record and show the first failed face.

\subsection{Inherited-authority obligations}

Some entries carry already established CM content.  They copy an installed terminal packet, an authority surface, a generated carrier, or a face-exhaustion result.  They do not introduce a fresh terminal object for the paper to test.

Their mathematical role is restraint.  An inherited-authority entry contributes through the theorem or face sweep it inherits from.  It supplies no fourth membership requirement and no new continuation branch.  The manuscript keeps these entries visible so the reader can see why already-paid material is not being counted again as an independent terminal alternative.

\subsection{Pack-face terminal obligations}

Pack-face obligations are the branches whose selected terminal object loses the same-fluid carrier first.  The mechanisms include carrier loss, cover loss, packing failure, failed retained-packet admission, and Pack bridge failure.  Their closing statement is
\[
  \neg\Pack_Q\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\Exit(Q;\Owork).
\]
A member record has to be carried by a positive same-fluid packet before participation and field readout can even be asked.  When that carrier is absent, the branch exits at Pack.

This family handles bare terminal atoms, detached source objects, failed packet admissions, and no-carrier endpoint readings.  The conclusion is not that the branch is visually singular.  The conclusion is that the selected record cannot enter the same-solution membership test.

\subsection{Part-face terminal obligations}

Part-face obligations keep enough carrier structure to pass Pack for the case split, then lose the same Navier--Stokes participation law.  The mechanisms include loss of the pressure-viscosity tether, failure of the participation envelope, dropped same-PDE law, and no-drop defects.  The closing statement is
\[
  \Pack_Q\wedge\neg\Part_{N,Q}
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \Exit(Q;\Owork).
\]
The selected record is still a carried object.  It no longer participates in the original pressure-viscosity-incompressibility tower through the derivative depth being tested.  The first lost membership datum is participation.

This family is where ``dead'' mechanisms belong when dead means loss of same-object dynamics.  The word is not a synonym for small velocity or no visible motion.  It names a Part-side failure of the original law on the selected carrier.

\subsection{Context-boundary obligations}

Context-boundary entries have no CM conclusion until they select a same-fluid terminal record or pay a named hinge.  They include history surfaces, audits, context material, downstream exports, readout statements, source recovery, manuscript presentation surfaces, supplier notes, and comparison material.  Their role is
\[
  \text{context}\quad\longrightarrow\quad
  \text{later Pack, Part, Field, membership-readout, or no-third-branch hinge}.
\]
They can strengthen the pass branch, sharpen the obstruction, explain why a witness matters, or prepare a later selection.  They remain context until the page identifies the selected same-solution record and proves either \(\Member(Q;\Owork)\) or \(\Exit(Q;\Owork)\).

This boundary keeps the appendix honest.  Useful material becomes proof only when the page shows the exact same-solution record it selects and the exact face or readout it pays.  Until then, it remains context.

\subsection{How the appendix is used}

The main paper uses these six families as a reader guide for the branch material.  A branch is closed only after it has one of the following forms:
\[
  \Member(Q;\Owork),\qquad
  \neg\Pack_Q,\qquad
  \Pack_Q\wedge\neg\Part_{N,Q},\qquad
  \Pack_Q\wedge\Part_{N,Q}\wedge\forall r>0\,\neg\Field_{N,r,Q}.
\]
Every other entry is context, inherited authority, obsolete material, or an open endpoint.  The appendix keeps the many branch names from overwhelming the proof route by making every live branch pay the same class-membership question.
\section{How Forward Material Enters the Proof}

This appendix records how forward-positive material enters the proof after the CM test has been fixed.  The repeated source files contain many local estimates and route probes.  The paper does not ask the reader to remember those file names.  It groups them by the kind of mathematical work they can pay.

There are four entry families:
\begin{description}[leftmargin=0.26\linewidth,style=nextline]
\item[Comparison context.]
Explains a nearby boundary object and then returns to the Navier--Stokes record.
\item[Export or legacy context.]
Preserves a result whose force is spent only through a named proof hinge.
\item[Forward supplier estimates.]
Pays source, carrier, participation, or readout costs for the selected branch.
\item[Receiver or endpoint readouts.]
Reads the selected packet after Pack and Part have already survived.
\end{description}
Each family becomes proof material at the point where it selects \(Q\), proves a face, or supplies the member-side readout.  Before that point, it is useful context and the proof says so plainly.

\subsection{Comparison context}

Comparison context is the material that shows why an obstruction shape is natural by placing it beside a neighboring equation or a downstream export.  Its admissible use is narrow.  A comparison may help identify a candidate packet, reveal a boundary behavior, or warn the reader that a route has changed equation class.  The class proof then returns to the same Navier--Stokes record:
\[
  Q_{\mathrm{NS}}
  \longrightarrow
  \Pack_{Q_{\mathrm{NS}}},\quad
  \Part_{N,Q_{\mathrm{NS}}},\quad
  \Field_{N,r,Q_{\mathrm{NS}}}.
\]
The comparison object carries no separate membership conclusion.  Its value is spent when the Navier--Stokes packet has been selected and the exact face or readout paid on that packet.

\subsection{Export and legacy context}

Export and legacy context preserves results that were produced for another surface of the project.  The current manuscript uses them through named hinges only:
\[
\text{terminal packet capture},\qquad
\text{membership readout},\qquad
\text{class exit},\qquad
\text{no-third-branch exclusion}.
\]
A legacy theorem that pays one of these hinges keeps its force.  A legacy theorem that only repeats a route label stays outside the terminal proof claim.  This rule protects the paper from treating an old status word as a theorem.

\subsection{Forward supplier estimates}

Forward supplier estimates are the gold-side material.  They try to pay the equation estimates directly: source reserve, donor refill, pressure residue, active-square production, terminal anti-atom control, annular residual load, shell gain, and high-frequency tail control.  When a supplier estimate succeeds, it can strengthen the member branch by producing a continuation readout.  When it reaches a precise obstruction, it can select the fail-side record tested by the CM proof.

The current live example is the annular supplier.  Gold asks for scale-uniform control of the residual load on every shrinking annular schedule.  The installed material has not written that gold estimate as a closed theorem.  The exact child left by the terminal pulse is \(\mathrm{TerminalTimeFaceAntiAtom.A}\), or the same-content new-production theorem \(\mathrm{TerminalNewProductionTheorem}_{B_{\mathrm{ASAC}}}\mathrm{.A}\).  Its checked entrances are temporal thickness or super-\(L^1_s\) source integrability; selected-source domination by a finite same-window reserve plus a terminal strip modulus; transported no-incoming flux together with terminal-face source-production exclusion; first-appearance upgraded into a time-priced ledger, source integrability, or a rigid no-atom subclass; and production of \(B_{\mathrm{ASAC}}\) into \(B_{\mathrm{ASAC}}^{TA}\).  The specific residual annular case is still exhausted: a gold pass removes the residual obstruction; the exact terminal time-face pulse explains why current inputs do not prove gold; a non-admitted diagnostic stays contextual or returns to the governing Pack boundary; and an admitted finite nonsmooth annular witness exits through Part or Field.

\subsection{Receiver and endpoint readouts}

Receiver and endpoint readouts read what remains after the object and law have survived.  On the pass side they supply a continuation norm, such as the \(H^s\), \(s>5/2\), readout used in the main body.  On the fail side they supply the Field alternative:
\[
  \Pack_Q\wedge\Part_{N,Q}\wedge\forall r>0\,\neg\Field_{N,r,Q}.
\]
This is why endpoint work belongs after the carrier and participation checks.  A good endpoint readout certifies the member branch.  A failed endpoint readout, after the same carrier and same participation law are still present, identifies the Field face.
\section{How Branch Families Pay the Proof}

The branch families are listed here so the reader can see how the current manuscript material is being carried by the paper.  The counts are coverage signals.  The proof role is the important part.  Each family either supplies a selected same-solution terminal record, pays one Pack/Part/Field face, pays the member-side readout, or remains an open context family.

\subsection{Source-reserve family}

This family accounts for the source-survival, zero-radius refinement, signed-current, no-free-sink, retained-amplitude, and terminal-atom material.  Its common object is a terminal reserve or source residue.  The class test begins only after that residue is attached to a same-fluid packet \(Q\).

Once \(Q\) is named, the proof route is fixed:
\begin{description}[leftmargin=0.30\linewidth,style=nextline]
\item[No positive same-fluid packet.]
This is \(\neg\Pack_Q\).
\item[Same packet, broken pressure-viscosity tower.]
This is \(\Pack_Q\wedge\neg\Part_{N,Q}\).
\item[Same packet and same tower, no positive readout scale.]
This is
\[
  \Pack_Q\wedge\Part_{N,Q}\wedge\forall r>0\,\neg\Field_{N,r,Q}.
\]
\end{description}
The source material is closed when one of these lines is written for the selected residue.  It stays open when it only says that some source pressure may survive.

\subsection{Local translator family}

Local translator material moves local \(L^3\), Duhamel, or public-critical mass onto a terminal packet.  Its job is not to prove smoothness by translation.  Its job is to preserve enough of the same solution record for the Pack/Part/Field test.  A translator that changes the pressure-viscosity law lands on the Part side.  A translator that preserves the law moves to Field and readout.

\subsection{Same-ledger family}

Same-ledger material asks whether the proposed terminal object is charged to the same witness record.  A preterminal reflection, imported donor, or exported branch has no membership conclusion until it supplies the same datum, same viscosity, same solution branch, same transported carrier, and same participation tower.  After those data are supplied, the object enters the ordinary witness tree.

\subsection{Class-law family}

Class-law material protects the pass-or-exit structure itself.  A reopening branch has to produce a genuine third possibility: an in-class nonsmooth terminal record that satisfies the membership data and still breaks continuation.  The current proof architecture sends such a challenge to one of three places: terminal CM entry, finite Pack/Part/Field exhaustion, or the no-third-branch closure.  A challenge that pays none of those places is support for a later audit, not a new branch of the proof.

\subsection{Local energy and elliptic family}

Local energy and elliptic estimates are analytic tools for selecting packets, verifying pressure participation, and reading positive field scales.  They enter the proof at the line where they pay one of those tasks.  For example, elliptic pressure control may help show that the same pressure law still participates on the carrier; local energy control may help keep the packet readable long enough for Field.  The estimate is proof material only at that paid line.

\subsection{Comparison-boundary family}

Comparison-boundary material is admitted only after it returns to a Navier--Stokes packet.  It can explain an Euler-like boundary, a fixed-viscosity loss, or a neighboring smoothness mechanism.  The class conclusion is still charged to the Navier--Stokes record.  The comparison family closes when the page writes the same packet, the shared carrier reading, the lost fixed-viscosity participation or field scale, and the resulting boundary interpretation.

\subsection{Candidate-branch family}

Candidate-branch material contains pressure tests and route probes.  It is deliberately provisional.  A candidate becomes part of the proof after it names a terminal packet and a witness face:
\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lll}
\(\Pack\) & \(\Part\) & \(\Field\)\\
member readout & terminal capture & no-third-branch exclusion
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Until then, the manuscript leaves it as an open continuation point.  That is a useful state for the paper, because the reader can see exactly which mathematical payment remains unwritten.
